properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 19 at 9:37AM PST until November 19 at 9:45AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
At 937 AM PST, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from 7
miles southeast of Llano to near Long Beach, or along a line from 7
miles west of Wrightwood to near Long Beach, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts. Small chance for a brief, weak tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Long Beach, Whittier, Pasadena, Mount Wilson, Carson, Port of Los
Angeles, Pico Rivera, Montebello, Monterey Park, El Monte, Santa Fe
Springs, Commerce, San Gabriel, Downey and Hacienda Heights.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds.
Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...

La Verne, Covina, Azusa, Baldwin Park, Diamond Bar, Hacienda

and Norwalk.

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 12:31PM EST until November 19 at 2:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 245 PM EST.

* At 1231 PM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 7 and 11 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Melbourne, Titusville, Rockledge, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Satellite
Beach, Cape Canaveral, Sharpes, Port Saint John, Port Canaveral,
Titusville Airport, Merritt Island, Playalinda Beach, Patrick Space
Force Base, Mims, Indian Harbour Beach, Jetty Park, Canaveral
Groves, Merritt Island Wildlife Refuge and Viera.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.instruction:

water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Total snow accumulations 6 to 12 inches. Locally
higher amounts possible on the Homer Bluffs, Diamond Ridge, and
along East End Road. Visibility reduced to as low as one half mile
in heavy snow.

* WHERE...SW Kenai Peninsula and Southern Kachemak Bay.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Thursday morning commute. Heavy wet snow may result
falling trees and tree branches. Heavy snow accumulations may
result in a few localized power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As of 7:45 AM, there have been reports of up
to 6 to 8 inches of snow accumulation in the Homer area with
snowfall rates of up to 2 inches per hour. Periods of moderate to
heavy snow will continue through mid morning before tapering off.
Increasing southwest winds this morning may result in localized
areas of drifting and blowing snow, especially at higher
elevations.
properties.instruction:

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 19 at 8:38AM PST until November 19 at 4:45PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin
River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and
San Joaquin Counties.

* WHEN...Until 445 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 836 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 1.2 ft above normal (6.1 ft MLLW) at 9:41 AM
Thu 11/19, 1.5 ft above normal (6.4 ft MLLW) at 10:07 AM Fri
11/20, 1.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 10:32 AM Sat
11/21, and 2.3 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:01 AM Sun
11/22.
* West Sacramento: 1.5 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 12:37
PM Thu 11/19, 1.8 ft above normal (6.2 ft MLLW) at 1:04 PM
Fri 11/20, 2.2 ft above normal (6.5 ft MLLW) at 1:35 PM Sat
11/21, and 2.5 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 2:09 PM Sun
11/22.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.4 ft at 12:00 PM Thu 11/19,
+7.0 ft at 12:00 PM Fri 11/20, +7.1 ft at 1:00 PM Sat 11/21,
and +7.3 ft at 1:00 PM Sun 11/22.
- These predictions include up to +2.0 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:30AM PST until November 19 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
At 830 AM PST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is up to 1
inch in 30 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by showers and thunderstorms. Debris
flows.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Long Beach, Downtown Los Angeles, Inglewood, Eaton Burn Scar,
Alhambra, Torrance, Pasadena, Manhattan Beach, Hermosa Beach, Redondo
Beach, Rancho Palos Verdes, Mount Wilson, Altadena, Carson, Eagle
Rock and Glendale.
properties.instruction:
Never drive through flood waters. Follow instructions from Emergency
Management and Law Enforcement.

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 11:29AM EST until November 19 at 1:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 145 PM EST.

* At 1129 AM EST, emergency management reported flash flood impacts.
Between 3.5 and 8 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall
amounts up to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Indialantic, Barefoot Bay, Roseland,
West Melbourne, Melbourne Beach, Grant-Valkaria, Micco, Melbourne
Shores, Floridana Beach, Spessard Holland Park, Melbourne Airport
and Eau Gallie.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:45 PM EST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:45 PM EST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:05AM PST until November 19 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
At 805 AM PST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 1 inch in
30 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses. Debris flows.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Palisades Burn Scar, Eastern Malibu, Encino, Pacific Palisades,
Brentwood, Interstate 405 through the Sepulveda Pass, Bel Air,
Topanga State Park, Sherman Oaks, Studio City, Mandeville Canyon,
Topanga Canyon Road through the Santa Monica Mountains, Coldwater
Canyon through the Hollywood Hills and Valley Village.
properties.instruction:
Never drive through flood waters. Follow instructions from Emergency
Management and Law Enforcement.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 19 at 6:29AM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This
includes the city of Seward.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM AKST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall is still on track to decrease late this afternoon.
Prolonged heavy rain may lead to areas of flooding along smaller
streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor drainage areas, and
ponding of water on roadways.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* WHERE...Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in Elko County.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Thursday morning and evening
commutes. Visibilities may drop below 1/4 mile due to falling and
blowing snow.
properties.instruction:

vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to
rise through Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage into
early next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the
river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Monday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

forecast.

properties.headline: Avalanche Warning issued November 19 at 5:29AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
AVWREV

The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S.
Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026

The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY
AVALANCHE WARNING for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002
(Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA))

* WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger exists in the backcountry. Large
avalanches are expected across backcountry terrain.

* WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49)
on the north and Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) on the south, including the
greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas,
not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs
exist.

* WHEN...In effect from Thu 05:30 PST to Fri 04:00 PST.

* IMPACTS...Significant amounts of new snow and wind are creating
dangerous avalanche conditions in the backcountry. The new snow is
overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas.
Avalanches could run down into treed terrain.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche
conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below
backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH
avalanche danger.

Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org
for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage
area of this or any avalanche center.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Placer, CA; Sacramento, CA; San Joaquin, CA; Solano, CA; Sutter, CA; Yolo, CA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 19 at 4:41AM PST until November 19 at 10:45AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Placer County in central California...
Sacramento County in central California...
Northwestern San Joaquin County in central California...
Solano County in central California...
Southern Sutter County in central California...
Yolo County in central California...

* WHEN...Until 1045 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 437 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain. This  will cause urban and small stream
flooding. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen in the
last 24 hours, with 0.1 to 0.3 inches in the last hour.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.7 to 1 inch are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sacramento, Stockton, Elk Grove, Roseville, Vallejo,
Fairfield, Vacaville, Citrus Heights, Folsom, Davis, Rocklin,
Woodland, Benicia, Galt, Carmichael, Fair Oaks, Rancho
Cordova, Lodi, West Sacramento and Lincoln.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 3:43AM CST until November 20 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 19 at 2:51AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
Bands of scattered showers and storms, on the north side of
developing low pressure, are expected to move inland across south
Florida today. The highest probability of being impacted by heavy
rain will be across Broward and Palm Beach counties today.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The metros of Miami-Dade and especially Broward and Palm
Beach counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread 3 to 5 inches of rain have fallen across the east
coast of South Florida over the past several days, with pockets
of 8 to 15 inches. Areas having received these higher end amounts
are most susceptible to today's forecast rain amounts. Common
rainfall amounts in locations impacted by showers will be 1 to 2
inches, with the isolated high end amounts closer to 3 to 5
inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued November 18 at 9:58PM PST until November 19 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
Between 3 to 6 inches of rain have fallen across the Santa Lucia
Range impacting the Timber and Plaskett Fire Burn Scars over the last
24 hours. Expect additional rounds of scattered moderate to heavy
rain impacting the Central Coast and Napa County through Thursday
evening.

* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Plaskett burn area and Timber burn
area.

* WHERE...For the Timber Scar, portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los
Padres National Forecast from Andrew Molera State Park to
Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur.

For the Plaskett Scar, areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile
marker 11 including Los Burros Road.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas is
expected during the watch period. Residents near the Timber burn
area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the
drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as
drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons.

Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential
debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks.

Be sure to stay up to date with information from local authorities.
Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas,
roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead
to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Big Sur, Plaskett, and Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 7:01PM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-
18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is
expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous
rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially
to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through
the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous
surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:

THROUGH AT LEAST THURSDAY MORNING

A moist and unstable air mass will bring the potential for
thunderstorms to the coastal waters. Any thunderstorm that forms
will be capable of producing locally gale force winds and rough
seas, dangerous lightning, heavy rainfall with reduced visibility,
and waterspouts..

properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Thursday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:21AM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING FOR THE UPSTREAM RELEASE OF PAINTED ROCK DAM ON THE GILA RIVER NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 AM MST TUESDAY

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 16 at 3:18PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole,
Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie,
and Martin counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast
through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast
with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest
potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal
counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM TUESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING
